desc: A spring engagement session at Sendall Gardens in Langley City: the best season, the prettiest corners, what to wear, the garden rules and how to plan it.

faq: Do we need a permit for photos at Sendall Gardens?

Not at the moment. The City of Langley says no permit is currently required for photography, as long as the group is 15 people or fewer, you don't set up props or decorations, you don't block the paths and you don't take over any area, including the greenhouse. Photo sessions also can't run during a booked wedding ceremony.
When is the best time of year for engagement photos at Sendall Gardens?
Spring is my favourite: from April into May the beds are full of colour and the light is soft. The tropical greenhouse is open from April 1 to October 1, and summer and early autumn are lovely too.
Can we get married at Sendall Gardens?

Yes, for a small ceremony. The Legacy Gazebo can be booked from April 1 to October 1 for up to 30 standing guests, in four-hour blocks, for $200 plus tax. The City asks for at least 10 days' notice and liability insurance, and there's no alcohol, amplified or live music, or confetti.
How long is an engagement session and what does it cost?
My engagement sessions are $225 for up to 60 minutes, with at least 30 edited images and a sneak peek within 48 hours. Sendall Gardens is small, so an hour is plenty to use every corner.
prose:
Sendall Gardens is one of Langley's quiet surprises: a small, free city garden of about 3.7 acres at 201A Street and 50 Avenue, with a creek, a gazebo, winding paths and a tropical greenhouse. In spring it's full of colour, and it's close enough to the rest of the Fraser Valley that it makes an easy, relaxed place for engagement photos.

This spring I photographed an engagement session here among the tulips, and every photo in this post is from that afternoon at Sendall Gardens. Here's what made it work, and how to plan your own.

A Spring Session Among the Tulips

We kept it simple: cream and white outfits, a slow walk through the garden and plenty of time on the benches between the flower beds. The bright spring colour does the work, so the two of you can just enjoy each other.

The Best Season

  • Spring (April and May): my favourite time. The beds are at their brightest and the light is soft.
  • Summer: long evenings and full green trees. Plan for the last hour or two before sunset.
  • The greenhouse: the tropical greenhouse is open to the public from April 1 to October 1.

The Prettiest Corners

  • The benches between the flower beds: relaxed, seated photos with colour all around you.
  • The paths along Muckle Creek: shade and soft light for walking photos.
  • Under the big trees: quieter, more intimate portraits.
  • The Legacy Gazebo: lovely when it's free, but it's booked for small weddings from April to October, so we work around those times.

What to Wear

Soft, light colours look beautiful against spring flowers: cream, white, blush and pale green. Avoid big logos and very busy prints. Bring comfortable shoes for the paths and a light layer, because spring evenings in the Fraser Valley cool down quickly. For more ideas, see my engagement outfit guide.

Garden Rules and Getting There

  • Permits: none are currently required for photos, according to the City of Langley.
  • Group size: 15 people or fewer.
  • No props or decorations, and no taking over any area, including the greenhouse.
  • Keep the paths clear for other visitors.
  • Weddings come first: photo sessions can't run during a booked ceremony at the gazebo.
  • Where: 201A Street and 50 Avenue, Langley City. I'll send you the exact meeting point with your session plan.

Rules can change, so I check the City's page before every session.

Plan Your Session

Engagement sessions are $225 for up to 60 minutes. I also photograph weddings and elopements across Langley and the Fraser Valley; see my Langley wedding photography page and engagements page.
